# .github/: CI workflows

## Scope
`workflows/ci.yml`: GitHub Actions for every push and tag, and manual runs. `actions/lfs/`: the Git LFS step every job but `release` uses. `rulesets/main.json`: the rule on `main` (pull requests only, all nine checks green on an up-to-date branch, rebase merge, linear history, no bypass). `dependabot.yml`: weekly updates of the pinned actions. `actionlint.yaml`: runner labels actionlint doesn't know yet.

## Rules
- Workflows only run `pixi run project_n <command>`; any logic beyond setup belongs in tools/project_n.py, so CI and local runs can't drift.
- Pin every action by commit SHA with the version in a comment; Pixi by exact version (`PIXI_VERSION`).
- Jobs split `check` so they run in parallel: `lint` (`selftest` with the `doctor --docs` check, commit-check, and `lint --container` over a branch's commits since main, or main's pushed ones; plus `fmt --check` over the same, which also catches commits made without the pre-commit hook), `container` (one clean-container `artifact` job per preset: build, tests, on Linux the reference pictures, dependency check, upload), `releasedbg` (linux-clang's `releasedbg` build in its container, the only mode with Tracy's zones), `windows` (native MSVC, one build per entry: `release` tests; `address`, ASan tests plus `selftest`), `macos` (native, one build per entry: `release` tests, then `artifact --reuse-build`, which packages that build on branch pushes and rebuilds in a clean room on main and tags; `address`, ASan tests), and on `v*` tags `release` (after all the others: `publish` drafts the GitHub release from every preset's archives). Locally, `check` stays the gate.
- One build per job on branch pushes (spec 2026-11-13 §5): a pull request waits for the slowest job, so a job that builds twice there is split, not given a second build. On main and tags `macos (release)` builds again for its clean-room artefact: the cold rule, not a job to split.
- Every push runs every job (the public repository's minutes are free), as does `pixi run gh workflow run ci --ref <branch>`. Never put an `if:` on a required job: GitHub counts a skipped job as passed, so the ruleset's check would be hollow.
- Never push or upload Microsoft's files (the MSVC install, anything from `/opt/msvc`): no image contains them, and only `dist/`'s zip archives are uploaded, named by `artifact` (`project_n-<version>-<preset>`, plus the commit unless a tag is built). Caching them in the Actions cache is accepted only because no workflow runs on `pull_request`: never add that trigger without keeping the MSVC caches out of it (the repository is public).
- Three cache layers. Setup, saved as soon as its step finishes: Pixi envs (setup-pixi), the linux and msvc images in GHCR by content tag, the MSVC install from `project_n image` (key: `msvc.Containerfile`), the native MSVC 14.50 toolset (key: `buildtools.vsconfig`), the macOS XMake bundle (key: `XMAKE_MACOS_SHA256`). Packages, saved at job end even on failure (never on tags, which write no cache): XMake packages per job (key: pixi files, `xmake-requires.lock`, `xmake/repo/`). Packages and objects save under the key their restore step computed (`steps.<id>.outputs.cache-primary-key`), never a fresh `hashFiles`: a build can change a hashed file (XMake adds a platform's missing entries to `xmake-requires.lock`), and macOS's object cache never hit while its save key drifted that way. Git LFS objects through the composite action `actions/lfs` (key: `project_n lfs-key`, a hash of the commit's LFS object IDs; a miss restores an older cache, then `project_n lfs-prune` drops unused objects before the save; Pixi's git-lfs via `project_n setup`, never `actions/checkout`'s `lfs`), in every job that builds or tests. Objects: compiled Clang objects (`PROJECT_N_BUILD_CACHE`, per job; `project_n` lays out the folders), in `lint`, `container`'s linux-clang entry, `releasedbg` and both `macos` entries (GCC stays off it: its PCH made stale objects; MSVC too, in `windows` and the windows-msvc container: Gotchas). Warm on branch pushes only: the restore step runs on branches, keyed on the pixi files, `xmake-requires.lock`, `xmake/repo/`, `xmake.lua` and the commit, so the newest earlier branch run seeds the next. Unlike the packages, the restore-keys keep that hash: XMake's object key holds the compiler path, not its version, so a toolchain bump must start cold. Main restores nothing (its restore step only looks the key up, `lookup-only`, so Save objects has one) and saves its cold build, which seeds a new branch's first run (branches fall back to the default branch's caches); tags neither (`project_n` enforces the cold rule itself: `cold_ref()`, `tag_ref()`). Saved at job end even on failure. A read-only Dependabot token only makes a save warn, as for packages.

## Commands
- Apply a changed ruleset (the user's say-so; it binds everyone): `pixi run gh api -X PUT repos/Lotus-Rob/project_n/rulesets/<id> --input .github/rulesets/main.json` (`pixi run gh api repos/Lotus-Rob/project_n/rulesets` lists the id)
- `pixi run gh run list --branch <branch>` · `pixi run gh run watch <id>` · `pixi run gh run view <id> --log-failed`

## Gotchas
- `actions/cache` saves only when the job succeeds, so a failing job rebuilt everything every run. XMake package caches use separate `cache/restore` and `cache/save` steps, saving even after a failure.
- No disk cleanup step: ubuntu-26.04 runners have ~90 GB free, and the images plus packages need ~25 GB. Deleting the preinstalled SDKs cost ~2 minutes per job.
- MSVC's objects stay out of the object cache (spike, 2026-11-14): XMake's `cl` cache compiles each file's preprocessed text without the precompiled header and keeps only the `.obj`, while `/Zi` leaves its debug types in the build folder's `compile.*.pdb`, so a warm windows-msvc artefact's `.pdb` shrank from 27.6 to 12.1 MB and its `.exe` matched neither the cold-cached nor the uncached build (two uncached builds give a byte-identical `.exe`; even cold, anonymous namespaces take the `__cpp_*` file's name). Under Wine it was no faster (`artifact` 445 s uncached, 683 s cold, 472 s warm: preprocessing a file costs what compiling it with the PCH does); native `windows` was (job 797 s, 464 s warm) but 342 s slower cold, as every `main` run is. Only `/Z7` would keep the debug info, a compile flag change to the release build, and the binary would still differ from an uncached one.
- Dependabot's push runs get a read-only token, so pushing a missing image to GHCR failed them, and with every check required its pull requests could never merge: `PROJECT_N_PUSH_IMAGES` is 0 for `dependabot[bot]` (ci.yml). Keep that condition when touching the expression.
